questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I lived at Broadway 777, which are dorms specifically for international students. It is managed by Mapleton Management and is very cheap compared to the rent prices in Boulder (500 usd a month all included + 500 usd deposit). The place is particularly nice, but very much cheaper than everything else, so I found it acceptable for 4-5 months. The building will be torn down in a couple of years time though. 

On campus housing is only for freshman and is not an option for exchange students. Generally people struggle a lot with finding affordable housing in Boulder and it was pretty difficult finding something. You can also go on Ralphies list to look for places, but most people want you to sign for a year. I had a friend who did this and then found someone to take over his lease, so that's also an option. Also if the deposit is not big, you can just leave obviously, but most landlords are fine if you find someone else to take over.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Boulder is not a huge city so you can get around pretty easily by bike (bike trails all over), so as long as you find something that's not on the outskirts of the city, you should be fine not being too far from campus. Also there are e-bikes (bcycle) that are free for one hour when you are a student of the university, which I used a lot

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
No problems at all, if a course is popular just make sure to sign up in good time as some classes get filled up though

Sign up for more courses than you need, you have something like 4 weeks to drop classes, at which point you can pick the ones that you like. As long as you have free electives the way I understand it, it doesn't matter too much with the pre-approval of classes you sent to KU

Look into signing up for intermural sports, I played soccer and broomball for two different teams. Really good experience, try somehow joining a team, it's really fun. Remember that americans are very open and nice to strangers

Also there is info meetings for various sports clubs that you can check out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
You can get a season ski pass (ikon pass) for 550 usd ish, through the ski club at CU boulder. There is a bus that goes from Boulder to Eldora (ski resort on the ikon pass). Eldora is not the best ski resort (still good), but the closest one (45 mins away). Other good ski resorts on the ikon pass: Copper mountain, Winter park, A basin and steamboat. All of these places are 1.5 hours away, except steamboat which is 3-4 hours away. So if you want to ski, get some friends with a car or buy a car. The best skiing is in january + february. I was there in the fall so not the optimal time for skiing, but still really good. I got 17 days of skiing with 2 powder days :)

For hiking if you don't have a car, go to the flatirons, which is walkable or by bus (which is free for cu students, just scan your card)

Also try and get a season pass for the football season (might only be in the fall), they get sold out pretty quick and tickets can be insanely expensive (depending on how the team is doing). It's definitely an experience going to a game

Boulder is a pretty fun place to go out, not a lot of dancing but very many good college bars. The average age in Boulder is 27, so it's a very young town. I would definitely be 21 before going on exchange to Boulder, you're not gonna get in anywhere unless you're 21, they ID everyone and are very strict. Most bars are on pearl street, and all places close at 2
